audit.whatIsWrong: Three strings claim Realm of Death takes Rumble's abilities away: spikes[1] 'Realm of Death removes your Equalizer, your Scrap Shield, and your escape', whys[4] 'Realm of Death removes Scrap Shield and Equalizer from the equation', mid 'Realm of Death strips away Equalizer, Scrap Shield, and your ability to disengage'.
audit.why: Realm of Death does not disable anything. It 'drags his victim to a different dimension with him and steals a portion of their stats'. Inside the realm Rumble keeps Scrap Shield, Electro Harpoon and The Equalizer — Equalizer is in fact a usable 1v1 zoning tool in a small closed arena. What is actually removed is his team and a slice of his own stats. A player taught that his shield is gone will not press it.
audit.corrected: Realm of Death isolates you and steals a portion of your stats — every button still works, you just have no team and worse numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in either layer states that Indestructible is charged by the damage Rumble deals. whys[1] only says 'he can absorb return damage'.
audit.why: Indestructible 'stores damage he deals and takes to create a shield. He may consume the shield to heal.' Rumble's entire damage profile is sustained tick damage from a 3-second Flamespitter cone plus burn, which is the single best way in the game to charge that shield. The longer the trade, the bigger the heal he converts it into — this inverts the 'force him to walk through your sustained damage' plan the mid text recommends.
audit.corrected: Your Flamespitter ticks charge Indestructible. Burst and leave, or force W out first; anti-heal cuts the conversion, not the shield.

audit.whatIsWrong: full phases[1] (Level 2) says 'Only take the trade when Mordekaiser's Realm of Death is down', and phases[3] (Levels 4-5) says 'trade around Realm of Death's cooldown'.
audit.why: Realm of Death is his ultimate and does not exist before level 6. Both phases are pre-6, so the advice is unactionable and hides the cooldown that actually gates those levels — Death's Grasp at 16/14/12/10/8s, the pull that sets up every isolated Obliterate.
audit.corrected: Pre-6 the tracked cooldown is Death's Grasp (16s at rank 1), not Realm of Death.
sources: champ-data/_kits/mordekaiser.json (E cooldown 16/14/12/10/8; R is the ultimate)

audit.whatIsWrong: 'late' says 'Use Flamespitter to zone him off objectives'.
audit.why: Flamespitter is a 600-range self-centred cone — it cannot zone anything at objective scale. The tools with the range to do that are Electro Harpoon at 850 and The Equalizer at 1750. The genuinely useful number here is that Realm of Death is only 650 range, so Mordekaiser must close inside Electro Harpoon's range to cast it, which makes the harpoon slow the actual peel.
audit.corrected: Peel with Electro Harpoon (850) — Realm of Death is only 650 range, so he has to come to you to press it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/rumble.json (Q range 600, E range 850, R range 1750)

audit.why: wants.foe[1] and wants.you[0] correctly build the lane around Obliterate's single-target damage bonus and the E-pull that isolates you for it — that matches 'Damage is increased when hitting a single enemy' and is the right shape for this lane.
50.63% over 879 games with a chart giving Mordekaiser levels 2-3 and 5-6 and Rumble the two-item window is consistent — the entry does not overclaim in either direction.

edits.before: Realm of Death removes your Equalizer, your Scrap Shield, and your escape — if Morde Rs you with Scrap Shield down, it is a free kill.
edits.after: Realm of Death takes your team, not your buttons — you keep Scrap Shield and Equalizer inside, but he steals a slice of your stats while it lasts.

edits.before: W shield comes online and he can absorb return damage while building Darkness Rise — short trades start favoring him and you lose sustained exchanges.
edits.after: W Indestructible comes online and it charges off damage he deals AND takes — pouring a full Flamespitter into it builds the shield he then eats to heal.

edits.before: Realm of Death removes Scrap Shield and Equalizer from the equation — the isolated 1v1 with Riftmaker sustain is one he wins cleanly when your shield is down.
edits.after: Realm of Death is a stat theft, not a silence: you keep every ability inside, but he takes a portion of your stats and no ally can trade the 1v1 for you.

edits.before: Levels 4–5 are a genuine contest — your Danger Zone Flamespitter deals serious sustained damage if you can force him to walk through it, but his E-drag punishes any overextension and his Q scaling starts chunking hard. The key discipline here is Scrap Shield timing: keep it banked whenever you step up to Q him, because the moment it is down he can E-pull you and fire an isolated Obliterate that swings the trade his way. At Level 6 the lane becomes outright dangerous — Realm of Death strips away Equalizer, Scrap Shield, and your ability to disengage, so if he Rs while your shield is on cooldown it is a free duel he wins with Riftmaker sustain. His R is your biggest checkpoint: track it like a kill button and never step up with your shield down in the window he can cast it.
edits.after: Levels 4–5 are a genuine contest — your Danger Zone Flamespitter deals serious sustained damage if you can force him to walk through it, but his E-drag punishes any overextension and his Q scaling starts chunking hard. The key discipline here is Scrap Shield timing: keep it banked whenever you step up to Q him, because the moment it is down he can E-pull you and fire an isolated Obliterate that swings the trade his way. Remember that every point of damage you land also charges Indestructible, which he converts straight into a heal, so anti-heal earns its slot the moment trades start going long. At Level 6, Realm of Death does not take your abilities — it takes your team, plus a slice of your stats — and the isolated 1v1 he drags you into is one he wins. Track it like a kill button.

edits.before: Late game is the one dimension where you reclaim relevance — Equalizer is a game-winning teamfight tool that functions entirely outside Realm of Death, and a well-placed line of rockets in a 5v5 can swing a fight without you ever needing to win a 1v1 against Mordekaiser. Your 1v1 is still a loss if he Rs you, so avoid isolated side-lane skirmishes and play through your team. Use Flamespitter to zone him off objectives and peel with double Electro-Harpoon if he tries to R a priority target. You scale into relevance through map-wide Equalizer impact, not through winning the sword-and-shield fight he wants.
edits.after: Late game is the one dimension where you reclaim relevance — Equalizer is a game-winning teamfight tool, and a well-placed line of rockets in a 5v5 can swing a fight without you ever needing to win a 1v1 against Mordekaiser. Your 1v1 is still a loss if he Rs you, so avoid isolated side-lane skirmishes and play through your team. Realm of Death is only 650 range, so he has to walk into your line — Electro Harpoon reaches 850 and its slow is your peel tool for keeping him off a priority target. You scale into relevance through map-wide Equalizer impact, not through winning the sword-and-shield fight he wants.

edits.before: Heat management is the kit: ride 50-100, never overheat by accident. Only take the trade when Mordekaiser's Realm of Death is down.
edits.after: Heat management is the kit: ride 50-100, never overheat by accident. Realm of Death does not exist yet — trade around Death's Grasp.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Realm of Death's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: The lane-control window: trade around Death's Grasp, 16s at rank 1, and bank leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.

notes: Packet flagged three suspect ability names here — 'Save Equalizer', 'Your Equalizer' and 'Use Flamespitter'. All three are FALSE POSITIVES as names (they are correct shorthand). I did edit the 'Use Flamespitter' sentence, but for a tactical reason (a 600-range cone cannot zone an objective), not a naming one. The 'full' layer for this matchup is generated boilerplate that substitutes the enemy ultimate into every phase string regardless of level — phases[1] and phases[3] both told the player to track a level-6 ability at levels 2 and 4-5. Worth checking whether the same generator bug affects every Rumble matchup, not just this one; I saw the identical pattern in rumble__mel.
